lesson.title: Text Length and Lines
lesson.driving_question: How can a program count characters and organise text across lines?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Measuring strings and arranging output with line breaks
lesson.concept_budget: Use len() with one string and the newline escape in output; iteration through text is deferred.
misconceptions: String positions begin at zero but length is a count.
Backslash-n is written inside a string.
The newline escape does not add visible characters to the displayed line.
lesson.progression_note: Adds two missing reference text operations before concatenation and character processing.
code_expectations: len() result stored in a variable

shared_program.filename: Text Length and Lines - Starter Code.py
shared_program.code:
message = input("Short message: ")
character_count = len(message)
print("Message:\n" + message)
print("Characters:", character_count)

trace.value: moves message to the next line

primm.prompt: Recall that a string can contain letters, spaces and punctuation. How many characters are in cat and red fox?
Use Code now. Count every character, including the space, and mark where the newline moves the displayed message.
Run with Code now and then with A B. Confirm that the spaces contribute to the character count.

questions: For the input Code now!, what number is stored in character_count, and which space or punctuation marks are included?
Why does the two-character sequence \n create a new line inside a string instead of appearing as two printed characters?
For the input Code now!, what appears on the line after Message:?

primm.prompt: Remove spaces from the start and end of the message before it is counted and displayed. Enter "Code now" with two spaces before and after it. The displayed message must be Code now and the count must be 8.

Ask for a title and store it in [title]. Ask for a subtitle and store it in [subtitle]. Display the title and subtitle on separate lines, followed by a labelled len() result for each one. Test "Code Club" and "Join today"; display "Title characters: 9" and "Subtitle characters: 10".

Ask for a poster heading and store it in [heading]. Ask for one instruction and store it in [instruction]. Display [heading] on the first line and [instruction] on the second line by placing \n between them. Add len(heading) and len(instruction), then display "Combined characters:" followed by the result. Test "Welcome" and "Sit here"; display "Combined characters: 15".
Repair the len() call and place the newline escape inside the heading string.

subtitle = input("Subtitle: ")

print("Subtitle characters:", subtitle_count)

instruction = input("Instruction: ")
total = len(heading) + len(instruction)
print(heading + "\n" + instruction)
print("Combined characters:", total)
